topics.title: Daniel Carver’s Malfunctioning Klan Machine
topics.summary: A man named Daniel Carver repeatedly calls into a radio show to discuss a malfunctioning machine that plays Ku Klux Klan messages. He blames various callers, including ‘pafafoui,’ for the damage and expresses racist views about Black people while seeking donations to repair it; other hosts attempt to engage him in conversation regarding his business venture.

topics.title: Brooklyn Yeshiva DJ Request
topics.summary: A caller requests Howard to book Ed McMahon as a DJ for a Jewish-Christian organization’s party at the Ritzaad yeshiva in Brooklyn. The event would involve playing ‘Hot Hot Hot,’ mimicking Scott's hand movements, and potentially featuring an insurance sales pitch from Ed McMahon.

topics.title: Ed McMahon & Baseball Mishaps
topics.summary: The broadcast features an interview with Colonel Clink discussing duty, followed by a chaotic exchange with Don Mattingly about baseball and bodily functions. The segment includes inappropriate questions regarding personal encounters within the catcher's box, revealing unprofessional behavior and awkward interactions among the hosts.

topics.title: Allen Encounter and Cookie Hunt
topics.summary: During a radio broadcast, host Howard Stern recounts seeing Woody Allen in disguise – wearing a large hat – while seeking cookies with Neil Mattingly. They express frustration over Allen’s actions and observe Mattingly's behavior as he attempts to obtain refreshments, leading to humorous exchanges about the situation.

topics.title: Stuttering John Interviews Earl Monroe
topics.summary: Stuttering John conducts street interviews with basketball legend Earl Monroe, asking questions about television appearances and other topics. Monroe responds with humor and compliments the show's hosts.

topics.title: Pizza Business and Delivery Work
topics.summary: A pizzeria owner from Glen Ridge discusses operating two pizza restaurants, employee training, and pizza preparation. The conversation includes anecdotes about delivery jobs, restaurant work experiences, and the economics of the pizza business.
